In [[mathematics]], the '''Tonelli–Hobson test''' gives sufficient criteria for a function ''&fnof;'' on '''R'''<sup>2</sup> to be an [[integrable function]]. It is often used to establish that [[Fubini's theorem]] may be applied to ''&fnof;''. It is named for [[Leonida Tonelli]] and [[E. W. Hobson]].

More precisely, the Tonelli–Hobson test states that if ''&fnof;'' is a [[real-valued function|real-valued]] [[measurable function]] on '''R'''<sup>2</sup>, and either of the two [[iterated integral]]s

:<math>\int_\mathbb{R}\left(\int_\mathbb{R}|f(x,y)|\,dx\right)\, dy</math>

or

:<math>\int_\mathbb{R}\left(\int_\mathbb{R}|f(x,y)|\,dy\right)\, dx</math>

is finite, then ''&fnof;'' is [[Lebesgue-integrable]] on '''R'''<sup>2</sup>.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Poznyak |first1=Alexander S. |title=Advanced Mathematical Tools for Control Engineers: Volume 1: Deterministic Systems |date=7 July 2010 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-08-055610-9 |page=352 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xo_bA8rczk4C |language=en}}</ref>
